decisions.choice: spoke ... saying: the formula that introduces God's words
decisions.reason: The same formula opens God's speeches in 6:10, 13:1 and 14:1. The words follow in verse 12.

source.text: שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי אֶת־תְּלוּנֹּת֮ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ דַּבֵּ֨ר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר בֵּ֤ין הָֽעַרְבַּ֨יִם֙ תֹּאכְל֣וּ בָשָׂ֔ר וּבַבֹּ֖קֶר תִּשְׂבְּעוּ־לָ֑חֶם וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: I have heard the grumblings of [the] sons of Israel. Speak to them, saying, between the evenings you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be satisfied [with] bread, and you will know that I [am] Yahweh your God.

en.L: "I have heard the grumblings of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel. Speak to them, saying, 'Between the two evenings you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be filled with bread, and you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.'"
en.B: "The grumbling of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} has reached {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ears. Tell them this: 'As evening falls you will eat meat, and in the morning you will have your fill of bread. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.'"
en.R: "I have heard the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} complaining. Tell them that at sundown they will eat meat, and in the morning they will have plenty of bread. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God."

es.L: «He oído las murmuraciones de los hijos de Israel. Háblales, diciendo: “Entre las dos tardes {{plural_you:comerán|comeréis}} carne, y por la mañana {{plural_you:se saciarán|os saciaréis}} de pan, y {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} que yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Dios”».
es.B: «Las murmuraciones de los israelitas han llegado a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} oídos. Diles esto: “Al caer la tarde {{plural_you:comerán|comeréis}} carne, y por la mañana {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}} pan en abundancia. Entonces {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} que yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Dios”».
es.R: «He oído las quejas de los israelitas. Diles que al ponerse el sol comerán carne, y que por la mañana tendrán mucho pan. Así sabrán que yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} su Dios».

fr.L: « J’ai entendu les murmures des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël. Parle-leur en disant : “Entre les deux soirs, vous mangerez de la viande, et au matin vous serez rassasiés de pain, et vous saurez que je [suis] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu.” »
fr.B: « Les murmures des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} sont parvenus à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} oreilles. Dis-leur ceci : “À la tombée du soir, vous mangerez de la viande, et au matin vous aurez du pain à satiété. Alors vous saurez que je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu.” »
fr.R: « J’ai entendu les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} se plaindre. Dis-leur qu’au coucher du soleil ils mangeront de la viande, et que le matin ils auront du pain en abondance. Alors ils sauront que je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} leur Dieu. »

sw.L: "Nimesikia manung'uniko ya wana wa Israeli. Sema nao, ukisema, 'Kati ya jioni mbili mtakula nyama, na asubuhi mtashiba mkate, nanyi mtajua ya kuwa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu.'"
sw.B: "Manung'uniko ya Waisraeli yamefika masikioni {{deity_pronoun:mwangu|Mwangu}}. Waambie hivi: 'Jioni ikiingia mtakula nyama, na asubuhi mtashiba mkate. Ndipo mtakapojua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ndimi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu.'"
sw.R: "Nimewasikia Waisraeli wakilalamika. Waambie kwamba jua likishazama watakula nyama, na asubuhi watapata mkate mwingi. Ndipo watakapojua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wao."

ko.L: "내가 이스라엘 자손의 불평을 들었다. 그들에게 말하여라. '너희가 두 저녁 사이에 고기를 먹고, 아침에는 빵으로 배부를 것이다. 그러면 너희는 내가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 너희 하나님인 줄 알게 될 것이다.'"
ko.B: "이스라엘 백성의 불평이 내 귀에 들렸다. 그들에게 이렇게 일러라. '해 질 무렵에 너희가 고기를 먹고, 아침에는 빵을 배불리 먹을 것이다. 그러면 너희는 내가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 너희 하나님임을 알게 될 것이다.'"
ko.R: "나는 이스라엘 사람들이 불평하는 것을 들었다. 그들에게 해 질 무렵에는 고기를 먹고 아침에는 빵을 실컷 먹게 될 것이라고 말하여라. 그러면 그들은 내가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 그들의 하나님임을 알게 될 것이다."

vi.L: "Ta đã nghe những lời lằm bằm của con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên. Hãy nói với họ rằng: 'Giữa hai buổi chiều các ngươi sẽ ăn thịt, và vào buổi sáng các ngươi sẽ ăn bánh no nê, và các ngươi sẽ biết rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} [là] {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời các ngươi.'"
vi.B: "Những lời lằm bằm của dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã thấu đến tai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Hãy nói với họ thế này: 'Lúc chạng vạng các ngươi sẽ được ăn thịt, và buổi sáng các ngươi sẽ ăn bánh no nê. Bấy giờ các ngươi sẽ biết rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời các ngươi.'"
vi.R: "Ta đã nghe dân Y-sơ-ra-ên phàn nàn. Hãy nói với họ rằng lúc mặt trời lặn họ sẽ được ăn thịt, và buổi sáng họ sẽ có nhiều bánh để ăn. Khi đó họ sẽ biết rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của họ."

decisions.choice: between the two evenings: at dusk
decisions.reason: The phrase means the time between sunset and dark, as when the Passover lamb was killed (12:6).

decisions.choice: you will know that I am Yahweh your God: the purpose of the gift
decisions.reason: God promised in 6:7 that Israel would know him as their God who brought them out of Egypt. The food in the wilderness will teach them this.

decisions.choice: has reached my ears
decisions.reason: Balanced puts "I have heard" as "has reached my ears"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: indirect speech
decisions.reason: Readable reports the message as indirect speech ("Tell them that ... they will") to avoid a quotation inside a quotation.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י בָעֶ֔רֶב וַתַּ֣עַל הַשְּׂלָ֔ו וַתְּכַ֖ס אֶת־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וּבַבֹּ֗קֶר הָֽיְתָה֙ שִׁכְבַ֣ת הַטַּ֔ל סָבִ֖יב לַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in the evening, and came up the quail and covered the camp; and in the morning there was a layer of the dew around the camp.

en.L: And it came about in the evening that the quail came up and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.
en.B: That evening, quail flew in and covered the camp, and by morning dew lay all around the camp.
en.R: That evening, so many quail came that they covered the camp. In the morning, the ground all around the camp was wet with dew.

es.L: Y sucedió por la tarde que subieron las codornices y cubrieron el campamento; y por la mañana había una capa de rocío alrededor del campamento.
es.B: Aquella tarde llegaron volando codornices y cubrieron el campamento, y por la mañana el rocío se extendía alrededor del campamento.
es.R: Esa tarde llegaron tantas codornices que cubrieron el campamento. Por la mañana, el suelo alrededor del campamento estaba mojado de rocío.

fr.L: Et il arriva, le soir, que les cailles montèrent et couvrirent le camp ; et au matin il y avait une couche de rosée autour du camp.
fr.B: Ce soir-là, des cailles arrivèrent et couvrirent le camp, et au matin la rosée s’étendait tout autour du camp.
fr.R: Ce soir-là, il est venu tellement de cailles qu’elles ont couvert le camp. Le matin, le sol tout autour du camp était mouillé de rosée.

sw.L: Ikawa jioni kware wakapanda, wakaifunika kambi; na asubuhi kulikuwa na tabaka la umande kuizunguka kambi.
sw.B: Jioni ile kware waliruka wakaja, wakaifunika kambi, na kufikia asubuhi umande ulikuwa umetanda pande zote za kambi.
sw.R: Jioni ile walikuja kware wengi sana, wakaifunika kambi. Asubuhi ardhi yote kuzunguka kambi ilikuwa imelowa umande.

ko.L: 그리고 저녁이 되자 메추라기가 올라와 진을 덮었고, 아침에는 진 둘레에 이슬이 한 겹 덮여 있었다.
ko.B: 그날 저녁에 메추라기가 날아와 진을 뒤덮었고, 아침에는 진 둘레에 이슬이 내려 있었다.
ko.R: 그날 저녁 메추라기가 얼마나 많이 날아왔는지 진을 다 덮었다. 아침에는 진 둘레의 땅이 이슬로 젖어 있었다.

vi.L: Chiều hôm ấy chim cút bay đến phủ khắp trại quân, và buổi sáng có một lớp sương quanh trại quân.
vi.B: Chiều hôm ấy chim cút bay đến phủ kín trại quân, và đến sáng thì sương đọng khắp chung quanh trại quân.
vi.R: Chiều hôm ấy chim cút bay đến nhiều đến nỗi phủ kín khu trại. Buổi sáng, mặt đất quanh khu trại ướt đẫm sương.

decisions.choice: quail: a small game bird
decisions.reason: Quail are small birds that fly in great numbers over the Sinai region on their yearly migration and often come down to the ground exhausted. God sends them again in Numbers 11:31-32 (see also Psalm 105:40).

decisions.choice: a layer of dew: the dew that fell with the manna
decisions.reason: Numbers 11:9 says the manna fell on the camp with the dew at night. The next verse tells what was left when the dew lifted.

decisions.choice: so many quail came
decisions.reason: Readable spells out that the camp was covered because the birds came in great numbers.

decisions.choice: "kware" for the quail
decisions.reason: "Kware" is the Swahili name of the quail, a small ground bird known in East Africa, so the bird can be named rather than left as birds in general. It is an animal noun and takes the animate agreement ("kware wakapanda").

source.text: וַתַּ֖עַל שִׁכְבַ֣ת הַטָּ֑ל וְהִנֵּ֞ה עַל־פְּנֵ֤י הַמִּדְבָּר֙ דַּ֣ק מְחֻסְפָּ֔ס דַּ֥ק כַּכְּפֹ֖ר עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up the layer of the dew, and behold, on [the] face of the wilderness, thin [stuff], flake-like, thin like the hoarfrost on the ground.

en.L: And the layer of dew went up, and behold, on the face of the wilderness [was something] fine, flake-like, fine as hoarfrost on the ground.
en.B: When the dew had lifted, the surface of the wilderness was covered with something fine and flaky, as thin as frost on the ground.
en.R: When the dew dried up, thin flakes were left lying on the desert ground. They looked like frost.

es.L: Y subió la capa de rocío, y he aquí, sobre la faz del desierto [había algo] fino, como escamas, fino como la escarcha sobre la tierra.
es.B: Cuando el rocío se levantó, la superficie del desierto quedó cubierta de algo fino y escamoso, delgado como la escarcha sobre el suelo.
es.R: Cuando el rocío se secó, quedaron en el suelo del desierto unas escamas muy finas. Parecían escarcha.

fr.L: Et la couche de rosée monta, et voici, sur la face du désert, [il y avait quelque chose de] fin, comme des écailles, fin comme le givre sur la terre.
fr.B: Quand la rosée se fut levée, la surface du désert était couverte de quelque chose de fin, en flocons, mince comme le givre sur le sol.
fr.R: Quand la rosée a séché, il est resté sur le sol du désert de petits flocons très fins. On aurait dit du givre.

sw.L: Nalo tabaka la umande likapanda, na tazama, juu ya uso wa jangwa [palikuwa na kitu] chembamba, kama magamba, chembamba kama jalidi juu ya nchi.
sw.B: Umande ulipoondoka, uso wa jangwa ulikuwa umefunikwa na vitu vyembamba kama magamba, vyembamba kama jalidi juu ya ardhi.
sw.R: Umande ulipokauka, vipande vidogo vyembamba vilibaki juu ya ardhi ya jangwa. Vilionekana kama barafu nyembamba.

ko.L: 그리고 그 이슬 층이 걷히자, 보아라, 광야 표면에 가늘고 비늘 같은 것이, 땅 위의 서리처럼 가는 것이 [있었다].
ko.B: 이슬이 걷히고 나니, 광야 바닥에 서리처럼 가늘고 얇은 조각 같은 것이 덮여 있었다.
ko.R: 이슬이 마르자 광야 땅 위에 얇은 조각들이 남아 있었다. 그것은 서리처럼 보였다.

vi.L: Khi lớp sương tan đi, kìa, trên mặt hoang mạc [có vật gì] nhỏ mịn, như vảy, mịn như sương muối trên mặt đất.
vi.B: Khi sương tan, trên mặt hoang mạc có một thứ gì nhỏ mịn như vảy, mỏng như sương giá trên mặt đất.
vi.R: Khi sương khô đi, trên mặt đất trong hoang mạc còn lại những mảnh nhỏ mỏng. Trông chúng giống như sương giá.

decisions.choice: flake-like: flaky, or perhaps scaly or round
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here in the Bible, so its meaning is not certain. It is usually taken to mean flaky or scale-like; some take it as round, in the way coriander seed is round (verse 31).

decisions.choice: fine ... as hoarfrost: thin and white like frost
decisions.reason: "Fine" means thin or small. Hoarfrost is the white frost that forms on the ground in a cold night (Psalm 147:16).

decisions.choice: They looked like frost.
decisions.reason: Readable splits the description into two short sentences.

decisions.choice: "jalidi" for the hoarfrost (L, B); "barafu nyembamba" (thin ice) at Readable
decisions.reason: "Jalidi" is the standard word for frost, but frost is rare in most Swahili-speaking lands and many readers will not know the word, so Readable describes it as thin ice. "Theluji" is snow, which would make the flakes too thick.

source.text: וַיִּרְא֣וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ אִ֤ישׁ אֶל־אָחִיו֙ מָ֣ן ה֔וּא כִּ֛י לֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ מַה־ה֑וּא וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם ה֣וּא הַלֶּ֔חֶם אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה לָכֶ֖ם לְאָכְלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw [the] sons of Israel and said each to his brother, what [is] it? For not they knew what it [was]. And said Moses to them, it [is] the bread that has given Yahweh to you for food.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel saw [it], and they said one to another, "What [is] it?" for they did not know what it [was]. And Moses said to them, "It [is] the bread that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given you for food.
en.B: "What is it?" the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} asked one another when they saw it, since they did not know what it was. Moses answered them, "It is bread, given to you by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as your food.
en.R: When the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} saw it, they asked each other, "What is it?" They had no idea what it was. Moses told them, "This is the bread {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given you to eat.

es.L: Y [lo] vieron los hijos de Israel, y se dijeron unos a otros: «¿Qué [es] esto?», porque no sabían qué [era]. Y les dijo Moisés: «Es el pan que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:les|os}} ha dado por alimento.
es.B: «¿Qué es esto?», se preguntaron unos a otros los israelitas al verlo, porque no sabían lo que era. Moisés les respondió: «Es pan, el que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:les|os}} ha dado como alimento.
es.R: Cuando los israelitas lo vieron, se preguntaron unos a otros: «¿Qué es esto?». No tenían ni idea de lo que era. Moisés les dijo: «Este es el pan que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:les|os}} ha dado para comer.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël [le] virent, et ils se dirent l’un à l’autre : « Qu’[est-ce que] cela ? » car ils ne savaient pas ce que c’[était]. Et Moïse leur dit : « C’[est] le pain que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous a donné pour nourriture.
fr.B: « Qu’est-ce que c’est ? » se demandèrent les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} en le voyant, car ils ne savaient pas ce que c’était. Moïse leur répondit : « C’est du pain, que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous a donné pour nourriture.
fr.R: Quand les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} l’ont vu, ils se sont demandé les uns aux autres : « Qu’est-ce que c’est ? » Ils ne savaient pas du tout ce que c’était. Moïse leur a dit : « C’est le pain que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous a donné à manger.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wakaona, wakaambiana kila mtu na ndugu yake, "[Ni] nini hiki?" kwa maana hawakujua [ni] nini. Naye Musa akawaambia, "Huu [ni] mkate ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewapa kuwa chakula.
sw.B: "Hiki ni nini?" Waisraeli waliulizana walipokiona, kwa kuwa hawakujua kilikuwa nini. Musa akawajibu, "Huu ni mkate, ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewapa kuwa chakula chenu.
sw.R: Waisraeli walipokiona, waliulizana, "Ni nini hiki?" Hawakujua kabisa kilikuwa kitu gani. Musa akawaambia, "Huu ndio mkate ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewapa mle.

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘 자손이 [그것을] 보고 서로 "이것이 무엇이냐?" 하고 말하였다. 그것이 무엇인지 몰랐기 때문이다. 그러자 모세가 그들에게 말하였다. "그것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희에게 먹으라고 주신 빵이다.
ko.B: 이스라엘 백성은 그것을 보고 "이것이 무엇이냐?" 하고 서로 물었다. 그것이 무엇인지 알지 못하였기 때문이다. 모세가 그들에게 대답하였다. "이것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희에게 먹으라고 주신 빵이다.
ko.R: 이스라엘 사람들은 그것을 보고 "이것이 뭐지?" 하고 서로 물었다. 그것이 무엇인지 아무도 몰랐다. 모세가 그들에게 말했다. "이것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 여러분에게 먹으라고 주신 빵입니다.

vi.L: Con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên thấy [nó], và họ nói với nhau: "Cái gì [đây]?" vì họ không biết đó [là] gì. Môi-se nói với họ: "Đó [là] bánh {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã ban cho các ngươi làm thức ăn.
vi.B: Khi thấy vậy, dân Y-sơ-ra-ên hỏi nhau: "Cái gì đây?" vì họ không biết đó là gì. Môi-se đáp: "Đó là bánh {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban cho anh em làm thức ăn.
vi.R: Khi dân Y-sơ-ra-ên thấy thứ ấy, họ hỏi nhau: "Cái gì đây?" Họ không biết đó là gì. Môi-se bảo họ: "Đây là bánh {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban cho anh em ăn.

decisions.choice: What is it?: a word-play on the name manna
alternatives: it is manna (taking the word as the name already)
decisions.reason: The people ask "What is it?" with a rare word for "what" that sounds the same as the name the food is given in verse 31, "manna". The word appears to be an old or regional form, which the narrator explains at once with the ordinary word for "what" ("they did not know what it was"). So the name manna recalls the question: the food was named after the people's puzzlement.

decisions.choice: the bread that Yahweh has given you: the promised bread from heaven
decisions.reason: Moses names the strange flakes as the bread God promised in verse 4. Jesus takes this up in John 6:31-35.

decisions.choice: "What is it?" first
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the question first, so that the words the name comes from stand out.

decisions.choice: "이것이 무엇이냐?" with no attempt to copy the Hebrew sound
decisions.reason: The question plays on the name manna (meaning decision, footnoted); Korean cannot reproduce the sound, so the footnote carries the wordplay, and 16:31 gives the name.

decisions.choice: "Cái gì đây?" for the people's question
decisions.reason: The question sounds like the name "manna" in Hebrew (meaning decision, footnoted); Vietnamese cannot keep the wordplay in the text, so it gives the plain question and leaves the link to the footnote and to verse 31.

source.text: זֶ֤ה הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה לִקְט֣וּ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ אִ֖ישׁ לְפִ֣י אָכְל֑וֹ עֹ֣מֶר לַגֻּלְגֹּ֗לֶת מִסְפַּר֙ נַפְשֹׁ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם אִ֛ישׁ לַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּאָהֳל֖וֹ תִּקָּֽחוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: This [is] the word that has commanded Yahweh: gather of it each to [the] mouth of his eating, an omer for a head, [the] number of your persons, each for [those] who [are] in his tent you will take.

en.L: This [is] the thing that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded: 'Gather of it, {{gender:each one|each man}} according to {{gender:their|his}} eating, an omer per head, [by] the number of your persons; you shall take, each man for those in his tent.'"
en.B: Here is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded: 'Each of you is to gather as much as you need to eat, {{units:about 2 quarts|an omer}} for every person. The head of each household is to collect it for everyone who lives in his tent.'"
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded you to gather as much as you need to eat. Take {{units:about 2 quarts|an omer}} for each person. Collect it for everyone who lives in your tent."

es.L: Esto [es] lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha mandado: “Recoja de él cada uno según lo que coma, un ómer por cabeza, según el número de {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} personas; cada uno tomará para los que [están] en su tienda”».
es.B: Esto es lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha ordenado: “Cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} debe recoger lo que necesite para comer, {{units:unos 2 litros|un ómer}} por persona. El jefe de cada familia lo recogerá para todos los que viven en su tienda”».
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:les|os}} ha ordenado recoger todo lo que {{plural_you:necesiten|necesitéis}} para comer. {{plural_you:Tomen|Tomad}} {{units:unos 2 litros|un ómer}} por persona. {{plural_you:Recójanlo|Recogedlo}} para todos los que viven en {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} tienda».

fr.L: Voici la chose que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a ordonnée : “Ramassez-en, chacun selon ce qu’il mange, un omer par tête, selon le nombre de vos personnes ; vous [en] prendrez chacun pour ceux qui sont dans sa tente.” »
fr.B: Voici ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a ordonné : “Que chacun de vous en ramasse autant qu’il lui faut pour manger, {{units:environ 2 litres|un omer}} par personne. Le chef de chaque famille en ramassera pour tous ceux qui vivent sous sa tente.” »
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous a ordonné d’en ramasser autant qu’il vous faut pour manger. Prenez {{units:environ 2 litres|un omer}} pour chaque personne. Ramassez-en pour tous ceux qui vivent sous votre tente. »

sw.L: Hili [ndilo] neno ambalo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameamuru: 'Okoteni sehemu yake, kila mtu kwa kadiri ya ulaji wake, omeri moja kwa kila kichwa, kwa hesabu ya watu wenu; kila mtu atatwaa kwa ajili ya wale walio katika hema lake.'"
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyoamuru: 'Kila mmoja wenu aokote kiasi anachohitaji kula, {{units:kama lita 2|omeri moja}} kwa kila mtu. Mkuu wa kila jamaa atawaokotea wote wanaoishi katika hema lake.'"
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameagiza mwokote kiasi mnachohitaji kula. Chukueni {{units:kama lita 2|omeri moja}} kwa kila mtu. Okoteni kwa ajili ya kila mtu anayeishi katika hema lenu."

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 명령하신 것은 이것이다. '너희는 저마다 먹을 만큼 그것을 거두되, 너희 식구 수대로 한 사람에 한 오멜씩, 저마다 자기 장막에 있는 사람들을 위하여 거두어라.'"
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 명령하셨다. '너희는 저마다 먹을 만큼 거두되, 한 사람에 {{units:2.2리터쯤|한 오멜}}씩 거두어라. 가장은 자기 장막에 사는 식구 수대로 거두어라.'"
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 여러분에게 먹을 만큼 거두라고 명령하셨습니다. 한 사람에 {{units:2.2리터쯤|한 오멜}}씩 거두십시오. 여러분의 장막에 사는 사람 수대로 거두십시오."

vi.L: Đây [là] điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền: 'Hãy lượm lấy nó, mỗi người theo sức ăn của mình, mỗi đầu người một ô-me, theo số người của các ngươi; mỗi người phải lấy cho những người trong lều mình.'"
vi.B: Đây là điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền: 'Mỗi người hãy lượm theo nhu cầu ăn của mình, mỗi người {{units:khoảng 2 lít|một ô-me}}. Người chủ nhà phải lượm cho mọi người sống trong lều của mình.'"
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} truyền cho anh em phải lượm vừa đủ ăn. Mỗi người lấy {{units:khoảng 2 lít|một ô-me}}. Hãy lượm cho mọi người sống trong lều của anh em."

decisions.choice: omer: a dry measure, about two quarts
decisions.reason: The omer is a measure for grain and dry food, a tenth of an ephah (verse 36). It held roughly two quarts (about two liters), a day's food for one person. The word is used for this measure only in this chapter.

decisions.choice: according to the mouth of his eating: as much as each one eats
decisions.reason: "To the mouth of" means "in proportion to". Each person is to gather what he or she needs (also verses 18 and 21).

decisions.choice: each man for those in his tent: the head of each household
decisions.reason: One person, the head of the household, gathered for everyone who lived in the family tent, an omer for each of them.

decisions.choice: {{units:about 2 quarts|an omer}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern measure, with "omer" as the reader's alternative. Literal keeps "omer".

decisions.choice: indirect speech
decisions.reason: Readable reports the command as indirect speech, since Moses is already speaking.

decisions.choice: "ómer" (plural "ómeres") for the measure, in this chapter
decisions.reason: "Ómer" is the Hebrew name written as Spanish; "gomer", the older Spanish Bible form, comes through the Latin "gomor" and is less clear today.

decisions.choice: "omeri" for the measure, with a Swahili final vowel
decisions.reason: "Pishi" and "kibaba" are Swahili dry measures of a different size, so using them would give a wrong amount. The Hebrew name is kept, as for other measures ("shekeli", "efa"), and the units setting gives the metric amount at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: {{units:2.2리터쯤|한 오멜}}: metric by default, the omer as the alternative; Literal keeps "오멜"
decisions.reason: Korean readers measure in litres, so the default is metric (an omer is about 2.2 litres, the value the Pentateuch sheets use), where the English default is US quarts. This holds for these chapters.

decisions.choice: "khoảng 2 lít" by default, "một ô-me" as the units alternative
decisions.reason: As in the other Old Testament books in Vietnamese, measures are metric by default with the original unit as the alternative; the English converts to US quarts. The figure follows the English and the other languages in this chapter (about 2); the term sheet's 2.2 litres rounds to it. Literal keeps "ô-me", and "mỗi người" needs no gender span.

source.text: וַיַּעֲשׂוּ־כֵ֖ן בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיִּלְקְט֔וּ הַמַּרְבֶּ֖ה וְהַמַּמְעִֽיט׃

records.literal_gloss: And did so [the] sons of Israel, and they gathered, the [one who] made much and the [one who] made little.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel did so, and they gathered, the one [gathering] much and the one [gathering] little.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did this. Some of them gathered a lot, and others only a little.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did what they were told. Some gathered more, and some gathered less.

es.L: E hicieron así los hijos de Israel, y recogieron, el que [recogía] mucho y el que [recogía] poco.
es.B: Los israelitas lo hicieron así. Unos recogieron mucho, y otros solo un poco.
es.R: Los israelitas hicieron lo que se les había dicho. Algunos recogieron más, y otros menos.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël firent ainsi, et ils ramassèrent, celui [qui ramassait] beaucoup et celui [qui ramassait] peu.
fr.B: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} firent ainsi. Les uns en ramassèrent beaucoup, les autres peu.
fr.R: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont fait ce qu’on leur avait dit. Certains en ont ramassé plus, d’autres moins.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wakafanya hivyo, wakaokota, mwenye [kuokota] kingi na mwenye [kuokota] kidogo.
sw.B: Waisraeli walifanya hivyo. Baadhi yao waliokota kingi, na wengine kidogo tu.
sw.R: Waisraeli walifanya kama walivyoambiwa. Wengine waliokota zaidi, na wengine kidogo.

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘 자손이 그렇게 하여, 많이 [거둔] 사람도 있고 적게 [거둔] 사람도 있었다.
ko.B: 이스라엘 백성은 그대로 하였다. 많이 거둔 사람도 있고 적게 거둔 사람도 있었다.
ko.R: 이스라엘 사람들은 들은 대로 했다. 어떤 사람은 많이 거두고, 어떤 사람은 적게 거두었다.

vi.L: Con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên làm như vậy, và họ lượm, người [lượm] nhiều, người [lượm] ít.
vi.B: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên làm như vậy. Có người lượm nhiều, có người lượm ít.
vi.R: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên làm theo điều được dặn bảo. Có người lượm nhiều, có người lượm ít.

decisions.choice: the one who made much and the one who made little: some gathered more than others
decisions.reason: The two words mean doing much and doing little, here gathering. Families of different sizes gathered different amounts, and some were simply more or less eager.

source.text: וַיָּמֹ֣דּוּ בָעֹ֔מֶר וְלֹ֤א הֶעְדִּיף֙ הַמַּרְבֶּ֔ה וְהַמַּמְעִ֖יט לֹ֣א הֶחְסִ֑יר אִ֥ישׁ לְפִֽי־אָכְל֖וֹ לָקָֽטוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they measured [it] by [the] omer, and not had surplus the [one who] made much, and the [one who] made little not lacked; each to [the] mouth of his eating they gathered.

en.L: And they measured [it] by the omer, and the one [gathering] much had no surplus, and the one [gathering] little had no lack; each had gathered according to his eating.
en.B: Yet when they measured it {{units:with a 2-quart measure|by the omer}}, the one who gathered much had nothing left over, and the one who gathered little had no shortage. All of them had gathered as much as they could eat.
en.R: When they measured it {{units:2 quarts at a time|by the omer}}, the people who gathered a lot did not have too much. The people who gathered a little still had all they needed. Everyone had gathered as much as they could eat.

es.L: Y [lo] midieron por ómer, y no le sobró al que [recogía] mucho, y al que [recogía] poco no le faltó; cada uno había recogido según lo que comía.
es.B: Sin embargo, cuando lo midieron {{units:con una medida de 2 litros|por ómer}}, el que había recogido mucho no tenía de más, y el que había recogido poco no tenía de menos. Cada uno había recogido lo que podía comer.
es.R: Cuando lo midieron {{units:de 2 en 2 litros|por ómer}}, los que habían recogido mucho no tenían demasiado. Los que habían recogido poco tenían todo lo que necesitaban. Cada uno había recogido lo que podía comer.

fr.L: Et ils [le] mesurèrent à l’omer, et celui [qui ramassait] beaucoup n’eut rien de trop, et celui [qui ramassait] peu ne manqua de rien ; chacun avait ramassé selon ce qu’il mangeait.
fr.B: Pourtant, quand ils le mesurèrent {{units:avec une mesure de 2 litres|à l’omer}}, celui qui en avait ramassé beaucoup n’avait rien en trop, et celui qui en avait ramassé peu ne manquait de rien. Tous avaient ramassé autant qu’ils pouvaient manger.
fr.R: Quand ils l’ont mesuré {{units:2 litres à la fois|à l’omer}}, ceux qui en avaient ramassé beaucoup n’en avaient pas trop. Ceux qui en avaient ramassé peu avaient tout ce qu’il leur fallait. Chacun avait ramassé autant qu’il pouvait manger.

sw.L: Nao wakakipima kwa omeri, naye mwenye [kuokota] kingi hakuwa na ziada, naye mwenye [kuokota] kidogo hakupungukiwa; kila mmoja aliokota kwa kadiri ya ulaji wake.
sw.B: Hata hivyo walipokipima {{units:kwa kipimo cha lita 2|kwa omeri}}, aliyeokota kingi hakuwa na kitu cha ziada, wala aliyeokota kidogo hakupungukiwa. Kila mmoja alikuwa ameokota kiasi alichoweza kula.
sw.R: Walipokipima {{units:lita 2 kila mara|kwa omeri}}, wale waliookota kingi hawakuwa na kingi mno. Wale waliookota kidogo walikuwa na chote walichohitaji. Kila mtu alikuwa ameokota kiasi alichoweza kula.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 오멜로 되어 보니, 많이 [거둔] 사람도 남지 않았고 적게 [거둔] 사람도 모자라지 않았다. 저마다 먹을 만큼 거두었던 것이다.
ko.B: 그런데 그것을 {{units:2.2리터들이 되로|오멜로}} 되어 보니, 많이 거둔 사람도 남는 것이 없었고, 적게 거둔 사람도 모자라는 것이 없었다. 모두가 먹을 만큼 거두었던 것이다.
ko.R: 그것을 {{units:2.2리터씩|한 오멜씩}} 되어 보니, 많이 거둔 사람도 너무 많지 않았다. 적게 거둔 사람도 모자라지 않았다. 모두 먹을 만큼 거두었다.

vi.L: Họ đong [nó] bằng ô-me, thì người [lượm] nhiều không dư, người [lượm] ít không thiếu; mỗi người đã lượm theo sức ăn của mình.
vi.B: Nhưng khi họ đong lại {{units:bằng đồ đong 2 lít|bằng ô-me}}, thì người lượm nhiều không thừa, người lượm ít cũng không thiếu. Ai nấy đều đã lượm vừa đủ ăn.
vi.R: Khi họ đong lại {{units:từng 2 lít một|bằng ô-me}}, thì người lượm nhiều không bị dư. Người lượm ít vẫn có đủ những gì mình cần. Mọi người đều đã lượm vừa đủ ăn.

decisions.choice: no surplus ... no lack: God made the portions come out even
decisions.reason: However much each household gathered, when it was measured there was an omer for each person, no more and no less. Paul quotes this sentence in 2 Corinthians 8:15 to urge believers to share, so that no one has too much or too little.

decisions.choice: they measured it by the omer: each household's gathering was measured out
alternatives: the surplus of some was shared with those who had less
decisions.reason: The measuring was done at home or in the camp after gathering. The verse does not say whether the amounts evened out in the measuring or by sharing; the point is that everyone had enough.

decisions.choice: {{units:with a 2-quart measure|by the omer}}
decisions.reason: As in verse 16, Balanced and Readable give the modern measure first. Literal keeps "omer".

decisions.choice: "많이 거둔 사람도 남지 않았고 적게 거둔 사람도 모자라지 않았다", worded as the Korean of 2 Corinthians 8:15
decisions.reason: Paul quotes this line; keeping the Korean close lets readers hear the link.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֲלֵהֶ֑ם אִ֕ישׁ אַל־יוֹתֵ֥ר מִמֶּ֖נּוּ עַד־בֹּֽקֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Moses to them, each not let him leave of it until morning.

en.L: And Moses said to them, "Let no one leave [any] of it until morning."
en.B: Moses told them, "None of you may save any of it for the next morning."
en.R: Moses told them, "Do not keep any of it until the next morning."

es.L: Y les dijo Moisés: «Que nadie deje [nada] de ello hasta la mañana».
es.B: Moisés les dijo: «Ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} debe guardar nada para la mañana siguiente».
es.R: Moisés les dijo: «No {{plural_you:guarden|guardéis}} nada para la mañana siguiente».

fr.L: Et Moïse leur dit : « Que personne n’en laisse [rien] jusqu’au matin. »
fr.B: Moïse leur dit : « Que personne d’entre vous n’en garde pour le lendemain matin. »
fr.R: Moïse leur a dit : « N’en gardez rien jusqu’au lendemain matin. »

sw.L: Naye Musa akawaambia, "Mtu yeyote asisaze [kitu] chake hata asubuhi."
sw.B: Musa aliwaambia, "Mtu yeyote kati yenu asibakize chochote hadi asubuhi inayofuata."
sw.R: Musa aliwaambia, "Msibakize chochote mpaka kesho asubuhi."

ko.L: 그리고 모세가 그들에게 말하였다. "아무도 그것을 아침까지 남겨 두지 말라."
ko.B: 모세가 그들에게 말하였다. "아무도 그것을 다음 날 아침까지 남겨 두어서는 안 된다."
ko.R: 모세가 그들에게 말했다. "아무것도 다음 날 아침까지 남겨 두지 마십시오."

vi.L: Môi-se nói với họ: "Không ai được để dành [chút gì] của nó cho đến sáng."
vi.B: Môi-se bảo họ: "Không ai được để dành chút nào đến sáng hôm sau."
vi.R: Môi-se bảo họ: "Đừng giữ lại chút nào đến sáng hôm sau."

decisions.choice: let no one leave any until morning: trust God for the next day
decisions.reason: This is the test of verse 4: each day's food is gathered on its own day, and no one is to store it up against tomorrow (compare Matthew 6:11, 34).

source.text: וְלֹא־שָׁמְע֣וּ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיּוֹתִ֨רוּ אֲנָשִׁ֤ים מִמֶּ֨נּוּ֙ עַד־בֹּ֔קֶר וַיָּ֥רֻם תּוֹלָעִ֖ים וַיִּבְאַ֑שׁ וַיִּקְצֹ֥ף עֲלֵהֶ֖ם מֹשֶֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And not they listened to Moses, and left over men of it until morning, and it bred worms and stank. And was angry with them Moses.

en.L: And they did not listen to Moses, and [some] people left [part] of it until morning, and it bred worms and stank. And Moses was angry with them.
en.B: But they would not listen to Moses. Some people saved part of it until morning, and it became wormy and foul-smelling. This made Moses angry with them.
en.R: But some of the people did not listen to Moses. They kept part of it until the next morning. By then it was full of worms and smelled bad. Moses was angry with them.

es.L: Y no escucharon a Moisés, y [algunos] hombres dejaron [parte] de ello hasta la mañana, y crió gusanos y apestó. Y se enojó con ellos Moisés.
es.B: Pero no quisieron hacer caso a Moisés. Algunos guardaron una parte hasta la mañana, y se llenó de gusanos y olía mal. Por eso Moisés se enojó con ellos.
es.R: Pero algunos no le hicieron caso a Moisés. Guardaron una parte hasta la mañana siguiente. Para entonces estaba llena de gusanos y olía mal. Moisés se enojó con ellos.

fr.L: Et ils n’écoutèrent pas Moïse, et [certains] hommes en laissèrent [une partie] jusqu’au matin, et cela engendra des vers et devint puant. Et Moïse s’irrita contre eux.
fr.B: Mais ils ne voulurent pas écouter Moïse. Certains en gardèrent une partie jusqu’au matin ; elle se remplit de vers et se mit à sentir mauvais. Moïse s’irrita contre eux.
fr.R: Mais certains n’ont pas écouté Moïse. Ils en ont gardé une partie jusqu’au lendemain matin. Le matin, c’était plein de vers et ça sentait mauvais. Moïse s’est mis en colère contre eux.

sw.L: Nao hawakumsikiliza Musa, na watu [wengine] wakasaza [sehemu] yake hata asubuhi, nacho kikazaa funza, kikanuka. Naye Musa akawakasirikia.
sw.B: Lakini hawakutaka kumsikiliza Musa. Watu wengine walibakiza sehemu yake hadi asubuhi, nacho kikajaa funza na kutoa harufu mbaya. Jambo hilo likamkasirisha Musa juu yao.
sw.R: Lakini baadhi ya watu hawakumsikiliza Musa. Walibakiza sehemu yake mpaka kesho yake asubuhi. Wakati huo kilikuwa kimejaa funza na kilinuka vibaya. Musa aliwakasirikia.

ko.L: 그러나 그들이 모세의 말을 듣지 않았다. [어떤] 사람들이 그것을 아침까지 남겨 두었더니, 벌레가 생기고 악취가 났다. 그래서 모세가 그들에게 화를 냈다.
ko.B: 그러나 그들은 모세의 말을 듣지 않았다. 몇몇 사람이 그것을 아침까지 남겨 두었더니, 벌레가 생기고 고약한 냄새가 났다. 그래서 모세가 그들에게 화를 냈다.
ko.R: 그러나 어떤 사람들은 모세의 말을 듣지 않았다. 그들은 그것을 조금 남겨 두었다가 다음 날 아침까지 두었다. 그러자 거기에 벌레가 가득 생기고 고약한 냄새가 났다. 모세는 그들에게 화를 냈다.

vi.L: Nhưng họ không nghe Môi-se, và [có] người để dành [một phần] cho đến sáng, thì nó sinh sâu bọ và hôi thối. Môi-se nổi giận với họ.
vi.B: Nhưng họ không chịu nghe Môi-se. Có người để dành một phần đến sáng, thì nó sinh dòi và bốc mùi hôi thối. Điều đó làm Môi-se nổi giận với họ.
vi.R: Nhưng có một số người không nghe Môi-se. Họ giữ lại một phần đến sáng hôm sau. Đến lúc đó nó đầy sâu bọ và bốc mùi hôi. Môi-se giận họ.

decisions.choice: it bred worms and stank: it rotted overnight
decisions.reason: The verb means to swarm or breed, with "worms" telling with what. The manna kept overnight was spoiled and rotten, against nature, for on the Sabbath it kept (verse 24).

decisions.choice: men: some people
decisions.reason: "Men" here means some of the people, not males only.

decisions.choice: some of the people
decisions.reason: Readable makes it clear from the start that only some did not listen, as the Hebrew shows by "[some] people" in the next clause.

source.text: וַיִּלְקְט֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ בַּבֹּ֣קֶר בַּבֹּ֔קֶר אִ֖ישׁ כְּפִ֣י אָכְל֑וֹ וְחַ֥ם הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ וְנָמָֽס׃

records.literal_gloss: And they gathered it in the morning in the morning, each according to [the] mouth of his eating; and grew hot the sun and it melted.

en.L: And they gathered it morning by morning, each according to his eating; and the sun grew hot, and it melted.
en.B: So morning after morning they gathered it, everyone as much as they could eat, and when the heat of the sun came, what was left melted away.
en.R: Every morning each person gathered as much as they needed. When the sun became hot, the rest of it melted.

es.L: Y lo recogían mañana tras mañana, cada uno según lo que comía; y calentaba el sol, y se derretía.
es.B: Así, mañana tras mañana lo recogían, cada uno lo que podía comer, y cuando llegaba el calor del sol, lo que quedaba se derretía.
es.R: Cada mañana cada uno recogía lo que necesitaba. Cuando el sol calentaba, lo que quedaba se derretía.

fr.L: Et ils le ramassèrent matin après matin, chacun selon ce qu’il mangeait ; et le soleil devenait chaud, et il fondait.
fr.B: Ainsi, matin après matin, ils le ramassaient, chacun autant qu’il pouvait manger ; et quand venait la chaleur du soleil, ce qui restait fondait.
fr.R: Chaque matin, chacun ramassait ce qu’il lui fallait. Quand le soleil devenait chaud, le reste fondait.

sw.L: Nao wakakiokota asubuhi kwa asubuhi, kila mtu kwa kadiri ya ulaji wake; na jua likawa kali, nacho kikayeyuka.
sw.B: Basi kila asubuhi walikiokota, kila mmoja kiasi alichoweza kula, na joto la jua lilipokuja, kilichobaki kiliyeyuka.
sw.R: Kila asubuhi kila mtu aliokota kiasi alichohitaji. Jua lilipokuwa kali, kilichobaki kiliyeyuka.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 아침마다 저마다 먹을 만큼 그것을 거두었고, 해가 뜨거워지면 그것이 녹았다.
ko.B: 그래서 그들은 아침마다 저마다 먹을 만큼 거두었다. 해가 뜨거워지면 남은 것은 녹아 버렸다.
ko.R: 날마다 아침이면 사람들이 저마다 먹을 만큼 거두었다. 해가 뜨거워지면 남은 것은 녹아 버렸다.

vi.L: Họ lượm nó mỗi buổi sáng, mỗi người theo sức ăn của mình; khi mặt trời nóng lên, nó tan chảy.
vi.B: Vậy sáng nào họ cũng lượm, mỗi người vừa đủ ăn. Khi nắng gắt lên, phần còn lại tan mất.
vi.R: Mỗi buổi sáng, ai nấy lượm vừa đủ những gì mình cần. Khi mặt trời nóng lên, phần còn lại tan chảy hết.

decisions.choice: in the morning in the morning: every morning
decisions.reason: Repeating a word means "each": every morning.

decisions.choice: it melted: the manna left on the ground melted
decisions.reason: What was not gathered melted in the heat of the day, so it could only be gathered early.

decisions.choice: what was left / the rest of it
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that it was the manna left on the ground that melted.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁ֗י לָֽקְט֥וּ לֶ֨חֶם֙ מִשְׁנֶ֔ה שְׁנֵ֥י הָעֹ֖מֶר לָאֶחָ֑ד וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ כָּל־נְשִׂיאֵ֣י הָֽעֵדָ֔ה וַיַּגִּ֖ידוּ לְמֹשֶֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was on the sixth day they gathered bread double, two of the omer for the one; and came all [the] leaders of the congregation and told Moses.

en.L: And it came about on the sixth day [that] they gathered double bread, two omers for each one, and all the leaders of the congregation came and told Moses.
en.B: On the sixth day they gathered a double amount of bread, {{units:about 4 quarts|two omers}} per person. All the leaders of the community came and told Moses about it.
en.R: On the sixth day they gathered twice as much food, {{units:about 4 quarts|two omers}} for each person. All the leaders of the community came and told Moses what had happened.

es.L: Y sucedió en el sexto día [que] recogieron pan doble, dos ómeres para cada uno; y vinieron todos los jefes de la comunidad y [se lo] contaron a Moisés.
es.B: El sexto día recogieron el doble de pan, {{units:unos 4 litros|dos ómeres}} por persona. Todos los jefes de la comunidad fueron a contárselo a Moisés.
es.R: El sexto día recogieron el doble de comida, {{units:unos 4 litros|dos ómeres}} para cada persona. Todos los jefes de la comunidad fueron a contarle a Moisés lo que había pasado.

fr.L: Et il arriva, le sixième jour, [qu’]ils ramassèrent du pain en double, deux omers pour chacun ; et tous les chefs de la communauté vinrent et [le] rapportèrent à Moïse.
fr.B: Le sixième jour, ils ramassèrent une double quantité de pain, {{units:environ 4 litres|deux omers}} par personne. Tous les chefs de la communauté vinrent en informer Moïse.
fr.R: Le sixième jour, ils ont ramassé deux fois plus de nourriture, {{units:environ 4 litres|deux omers}} pour chaque personne. Tous les chefs de la communauté sont venus raconter à Moïse ce qui s’était passé.

sw.L: Ikawa siku ya sita wakaokota mkate maradufu, omeri mbili kwa kila mmoja; nao viongozi wote wa jumuiya wakaja wakamweleza Musa.
sw.B: Siku ya sita waliokota mkate maradufu, {{units:kama lita 4|omeri mbili}} kwa kila mtu. Viongozi wote wa jumuiya wakaja wakamweleza Musa jambo hilo.
sw.R: Siku ya sita waliokota chakula mara mbili zaidi, {{units:kama lita 4|omeri mbili}} kwa kila mtu. Viongozi wote wa jumuiya walikuja wakamwambia Musa yaliyotokea.

ko.L: 그리고 여섯째 날에 그들이 갑절의 빵, 곧 한 사람에 두 오멜씩 거두었다. 회중의 모든 지도자가 와서 모세에게 알렸다.
ko.B: 여섯째 날에는 그들이 빵을 갑절로, 한 사람에 {{units:4.4리터쯤|두 오멜}}씩 거두었다. 회중의 모든 지도자가 모세에게 와서 그 일을 알렸다.
ko.R: 여섯째 날에 그들은 두 배나 많이, 한 사람에 {{units:4.4리터쯤|두 오멜}}씩 거두었다. 회중의 지도자들이 모두 모세에게 와서 그 일을 말했다.

vi.L: Vào ngày thứ sáu, họ lượm bánh gấp đôi, mỗi người hai ô-me, và tất cả các thủ lĩnh của hội chúng đến báo cho Môi-se.
vi.B: Vào ngày thứ sáu, họ lượm bánh gấp đôi, mỗi người {{units:khoảng 4 lít|hai ô-me}}. Tất cả các thủ lĩnh của hội chúng đến báo cho Môi-se.
vi.R: Vào ngày thứ sáu, họ lượm thức ăn gấp đôi, mỗi người {{units:khoảng 4 lít|hai ô-me}}. Tất cả các thủ lĩnh của hội chúng đến báo cho Môi-se biết chuyện đã xảy ra.

decisions.choice: came and told Moses: the leaders report the double portion
alternatives: they came to complain that people had gathered too much
decisions.reason: The verse does not say why the leaders came. They may have been puzzled by the double amount, since the people had not yet been told about the Sabbath (God had told Moses in verse 5), or they may have been asking what to do with it. Moses' answer in verse 23 explains it.

decisions.choice: leaders: chiefs of the community
decisions.reason: The word means one lifted up, a chief or leader, here the heads of the tribes or clans (Numbers 1:16).

decisions.choice: {{units:about 4 quarts|two omers}}
decisions.reason: As in verse 16, the modern measure comes first, with "omers" as the alternative. Literal keeps "omers".

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם ה֚וּא אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שַׁבָּת֧וֹן שַׁבַּת־קֹ֛דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָ֖ה מָחָ֑ר אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־תֹּאפ֞וּ אֵפ֗וּ וְאֵ֤ת אֲשֶֽׁר־תְּבַשְּׁלוּ֙ בַּשֵּׁ֔לוּ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־הָ֣עֹדֵ֔ף הַנִּ֧יחוּ לָכֶ֛ם לְמִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת עַד־הַבֹּֽקֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, it [is] what has spoken Yahweh: a sabbath observance, a sabbath of holiness to Yahweh [is] tomorrow. What you will bake, bake, and what you will boil, boil, and all the surplus leave for yourselves for keeping until the morning.

en.L: And he said to them, "That [is] what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken: 'A Sabbath rest, a holy Sabbath to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] tomorrow.' What you will bake, bake, and what you will boil, boil, and all the surplus lay aside for yourselves to be kept until the morning."
en.B: He told them, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said: 'Tomorrow is a Sabbath rest, a holy Sabbath to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.' So today bake whatever you mean to bake and boil whatever you mean to boil. Put aside everything left over and keep it for the morning."
en.R: Moses told them, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said: 'Tomorrow is a day of rest, a holy Sabbath day for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.' So today, bake and boil all you want. Save what is left over until the next morning."

es.L: Y les dijo: «Esto [es] lo que ha dicho {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: “Reposo de sábado, sábado santo para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [es] mañana”. Lo que {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}} a hornear, {{plural_you:hornéenlo|horneadlo}}, y lo que {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}} a hervir, {{plural_you:hiérvanlo|hervidlo}}; y todo lo que sobre, {{plural_you:guárdenlo|guardadlo}} para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, para conservarlo hasta la mañana».
es.B: Él les dijo: «Esto es lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha dicho: “Mañana es reposo de sábado, un sábado santo para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}”. Así que hoy {{plural_you:horneen|hornead}} lo que {{plural_you:quieran|queráis}} hornear y {{plural_you:hiervan|hervid}} lo que {{plural_you:quieran|queráis}} hervir. Todo lo que sobre, {{plural_you:apártenlo y guárdenlo|apartadlo y guardadlo}} para la mañana».
es.R: Moisés les dijo: «Esto es lo que dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: “Mañana es un día de descanso, un sábado santo dedicado {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}”. Así que hoy {{plural_you:horneen y hiervan|hornead y hervid}} todo lo que {{plural_you:quieran|queráis}}. Lo que sobre, {{plural_you:guárdenlo|guardadlo}} hasta la mañana siguiente».

fr.L: Et il leur dit : « C’[est] ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit : “Un repos de sabbat, un sabbat saint pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, [c’est] demain.” Ce que vous avez à cuire, cuisez-le, et ce que vous avez à bouillir, faites-le bouillir ; et tout le surplus, mettez-le de côté pour vous, pour être gardé jusqu’au matin. »
fr.B: Il leur dit : « Voici ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit : “Demain, c’est un repos de sabbat, un sabbat saint pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.” Faites donc cuire aujourd’hui ce que vous voulez cuire, et bouillir ce que vous voulez bouillir. Tout ce qui restera, mettez-le de côté et gardez-le pour le matin. »
fr.R: Moïse leur a dit : « Voici ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit : “Demain est un jour de repos, un jour de sabbat consacré {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.” Alors aujourd’hui, faites cuire et faites bouillir tout ce que vous voulez. Gardez ce qui reste jusqu’au lendemain matin. »

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, "Hili [ndilo] alilonena {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: 'Pumziko la Sabato, Sabato takatifu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [ni] kesho.' Mtakachooka, okeni, na mtakachochemsha, chemsheni; na ziada yote mjiwekee ili ihifadhiwe mpaka asubuhi."
sw.B: Aliwaambia, "Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyosema: 'Kesho ni pumziko la Sabato, Sabato takatifu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.' Basi leo okeni chochote mnachotaka kuoka na chemsheni chochote mnachotaka kuchemsha. Kinachobaki chote kiwekeni kando mkihifadhi mpaka asubuhi."
sw.R: Musa aliwaambia, "Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyosema: 'Kesho ni siku ya mapumziko, siku takatifu ya Sabato kwa ajili ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.' Kwa hiyo leo okeni na kuchemsha kadiri mnavyotaka. Hifadhini kinachobaki mpaka kesho asubuhi."

ko.L: 그리고 그가 그들에게 말하였다. "그것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하신 것이다. '내일은 쉬는 날, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 거룩한 안식일이다.' 너희가 구울 것은 굽고 삶을 것은 삶아라. 그리고 남는 것은 모두 너희를 위해 아침까지 간직하여 두어라."

decisions.choice: a Sabbath rest, a holy Sabbath to Yahweh: the first mention of the Sabbath in Exodus
decisions.reason: This is the first time the Sabbath is named in the Bible. The words come from a root meaning to stop or rest; the first word is a stronger form, a day of complete rest (31:15; Leviticus 23:3). The day is holy, set apart, and it belongs to Yahweh. God rested on the seventh day at creation (Genesis 2:2-3), and here, before the law at Sinai (20:8-11), he teaches Israel to keep the day by the way he gives the manna.

decisions.choice: what you will bake, bake: cook today what you need
decisions.reason: The manna could be baked or boiled (Numbers 11:8). The people are to cook today what they want, and keep the rest uncooked or cooked for the Sabbath.

decisions.choice: Yahweh's words: the announcement of the Sabbath
alternatives: Yahweh's words run to the end of the verse
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no quotation marks. Yahweh's words may be only the announcement that tomorrow is a Sabbath, with the instructions that follow given by Moses, or they may include the instructions as well. Either way the instructions come from God's command.

decisions.choice: a day of rest ... Sabbath day
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word Sabbath as "a day of rest" the first time it appears.

decisions.choice: "un repos de sabbat" for the stronger form shabbaton (L, B); "un jour de repos" at Readable
decisions.reason: The first word is a stronger form of the word Sabbath, a day of complete rest. "Un repos de sabbat" keeps the link between the two words that the Hebrew has; Readable explains, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "쉬는 날" for shabbaton and "안식일" for the Sabbath
decisions.reason: The term sheet sets "안식일"; shabbaton, a solemn rest, is said plainly, so the two words are not merged.

decisions.choice: "ngày nghỉ, ngày Sa-bát thánh" for "a Sabbath rest, a holy Sabbath"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's "ngày Sa-bát", its first mention in Exodus (meaning decision); "ngày nghỉ" says what the day is.

decisions.choice: it did not stink: kept by God for the Sabbath
decisions.reason: Manna kept overnight on other days rotted (verse 20). Kept for the Sabbath, it stayed fresh. The difference shows God's hand, not the nature of the food.

decisions.choice: maggot: a different word from the worms of verse 20
decisions.reason: This word means a maggot or grub, the larva that breeds in rotting food (Job 25:6). The meaning is close to "worms" in verse 20.

decisions.choice: "구더기" here, "벌레" in verse 20
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a different word here from the worms of verse 20 (meaning decision); Literal and Balanced keep them apart.

decisions.choice: "giòi" (L, B) for the maggot, beside "sâu bọ" (verse 20)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes that the Hebrew uses a different word here from the worms of verse 20; Literal and Balanced keep two words, while Readable says "sâu bọ" in both places.
